response.report:
EXAM: Chest radiograph, one view, 2026-11-20
CLINICAL INDICATION: Known lung nodule under surveillance. Admitted with fever. Portable film. Has the nodule changed?
ORDERING PROVIDER: Dr. S. Whitfield (synthetic), medical oncology
COMPARISON: Chest radiograph, 2026-08-21
TECHNIQUE: Current AP, prior PA. Projection differs from the prior. Current film is underexposed with heavy overlying chest wall soft tissue. Clavicles project high over the apices, suggesting a lordotic AP beam angle. Both films are mildly rotated. Patient position is not shown on either image. Comparability is limited (both reads).

LOOK AT FIRST:
- No finding is flagged time-sensitive. Priority order for review: F1 right lower zone opacity, F4 right hilar/infrahilar prominence, F2 right hemidiaphragm contour. Triage: urgency high, on-call page not triggered, needs human review.

FINDINGS (systematic read, done blind to the indication):
- Airway / lungs: Trachea is poorly seen on the current film, with no gross displacement. Hazy, ill-defined opacity in the right lower zone with apparent right basal volume loss, obscuring the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm, present on both studies (F1). On the current film the haze appears to reach the lower right mid zone. This may be explained by AP projection, underexposure and overlying soft tissue. F1 is indeterminate (both reads indeterminate). Left lung shows no focal opacity and no new confluent opacity. Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones on both studies (F6), stable by one of two reads. Density is not compared because of the exposure difference. No pneumothorax. No discrete, well-defined nodule is seen on the prior or current film. The prior report's nodular opacity (no side or zone given) is not matched to the images and not adopted. Small nodules cannot be excluded on the underexposed current film.
- Mediastinum / hila: Aortic knuckle is prominent with an unfolded contour on both studies, same shape and position. The upper mediastinum looks wider on the AP current film, which is expected with AP projection and is not called as a change (F5: indeterminate, the two blind reads disagreed, one read stable and one indeterminate). Right hilar and infrahilar prominence is continuous with the right lower zone opacity on both studies. Vessels, adjacent opacity and a hilar lesion cannot be separated (F4: indeterminate, raised by one of two reads). Left hilum is not clearly enlarged.
- Pleura: Lateral right costophrenic sulcus is aerated and pointed, while the medial right base is opaque. Subpulmonic or layering pleural fluid is not excluded. Left costophrenic angle is sharp. No pneumothorax. The prior report's small pleural effusion (no side given) is not confirmed on the images and not adopted. Right hemidiaphragm contour is high and indistinct medially on both studies (F2: indeterminate, the two blind reads disagreed, one read indeterminate and one stable). Apparent height differs with projection and beam angle, so interval change cannot be judged. Left dome is sharp. No free gas is identified, but the upper abdomen is underexposed on the current film.
- Heart: Cardiac silhouette appears prominent on the PA prior and enlarged on the AP current. The right heart border is obscured on both. AP projection magnifies the heart and size is not reliable (F3: indeterminate, both reads indeterminate).
- Bones / soft tissue: No displaced rib fracture or gross destructive bone lesion, but bone detail is limited on the current film by underexposure. Chest wall soft tissue is prominent on the current film. No soft tissue gas. No lines, tubes, pacemaker or other internal device on either film, and no new device since the prior.

INTERVAL CHANGE:
- Changed: No change can be called. The right lower zone opacity looks more extensive on the current film, the heart looks wider and the upper mediastinum looks wider. Each may be explained by AP projection, underexposure and overlying soft tissue, so none is reported as a change. Size and density change are not comparable across these films.
- Unchanged: The right lower zone opacity is present on both studies in the same location, with the same loss of the right heart border and medial right hemidiaphragm. Right hilar and infrahilar prominence is present on both. Aortic knuckle shape and position are the same. High, indistinct right basal contour is present on both. Left mid and lower zone coarse markings have a similar distribution (one read). No new device.

RECIST 1.1: not computed on radiographs

CAN'T DETERMINE:
- Has the right lower zone opacity changed in size or density since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP and underexposed. Projection and exposure differences can make a basal opacity look larger or denser. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able. (Read A, related to F1)
- Is there a right pleural effusion, including a subpulmonic component, and has it changed? | Reason: The high, indistinct right basal contour with an aerated lateral sulcus could reflect subpulmonic fluid, an elevated hemidiaphragm, or basal volume loss. A frontal film alone cannot separate these, and patient position on the current AP is not shown. | Recommend: Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest. (Read A)
- Is there a right hilar or infrahilar mass or adenopathy underlying the right basal opacity and volume loss? | Reason: The right hilum merges with the adjacent opacity on both films. Mild rotation and the AP projection make hilar size unreliable. | Recommend: CT chest, with contrast if appropriate. (Read A)
- Has heart size changed? | Reason: AP projection magnifies the heart, and cardiothoracic ratio is valid on PA films only. The right heart border is also obscured on both studies. | Recommend: Repeat PA film when the patient is able, or echocardiography if clinically relevant. (Read A, related to F3)
- Is the right hemidiaphragm truly elevated, or is the contour formed by subpulmonic fluid or a process below the diaphragm? | Reason: The true diaphragm is not separately visible on a frontal film. The lordotic AP beam angle on the current film also alters the apparent dome height. | Recommend: Ultrasound of the right upper quadrant and right base, or CT covering the chest and upper abdomen. (Read A, related to F2)
- Are there small nodules or fine interstitial changes in either lung on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underexposed with heavy soft tissue overlap, and the clavicles project over the apices. Small nodules cannot be confirmed or excluded. | Recommend: CT chest, or repeat PA and lateral with adequate exposure. (Read A)
- Has the heart enlarged since the prior? | Reason: Prior is PA and current is AP. AP projection magnifies the heart, and the right heart border is obscured on both films. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral when the patient is able, or CT chest. (Read B, related to F3)
- Has the right lower zone opacity grown, shrunk, or stayed the same? | Reason: Projection differs (PA then AP) and the current film is underpenetrated. Size and density change cannot be reported across these differences. | Recommend: Repeat PA and lateral with good inspiration, or CT chest. (Read B, related to F1)
- Is the high right hemidiaphragm contour a truly elevated diaphragm, a subpulmonic effusion, or lower lobe volume loss? | Reason: A frontal film alone cannot separate these. Patient position on the current AP film is unknown, and fluid layers out when supine. | Recommend: Lateral and right lateral decubitus views, ultrasound of the right base, or CT chest. (Read B)
- Is the upper mediastinum truly wider on the current study? | Reason: AP projection, possible mild rotation, and underexposure each widen or blur the mediastinal contour. | Recommend: Repeat PA film, or CT chest if there is clinical concern. (Read B, related to F5)
- Are there small lung nodules or a hilar abnormality on the current study? | Reason: The current film is underpenetrated and low in contrast, with overlying soft tissue shadows. Small nodules and hilar detail cannot be assessed, and the right hilum is partly obscured by adjacent opacity on both studies. | Recommend: Review the source image in PACS with windowing; CT chest if a nodule or hilar lesion needs to be excluded. (Read B)
- Is there a retrocardiac opacity? | Reason: Vertebrae are not visible behind the heart on the current film, and a frontal view alone cannot clear this area. | Recommend: Lateral view or CT chest. (Read B)

IMPRESSION:
1. Hazy right lower zone opacity with apparent right basal volume loss, present on both studies (F1). Indeterminate. Size and density change cannot be judged because the prior is PA and the current is an underexposed AP. A new process within it can be neither confirmed nor excluded.
2. Right hilar and infrahilar prominence continuous with the right lower zone opacity (F4). Indeterminate. Hilar size and change cannot be judged. Only one of the two reads raised this finding.
3. High right hemidiaphragm contour, indistinct medially, on both studies (F2). Indeterminate. The two blind reads disagreed (indeterminate versus stable). Subpulmonic fluid is not excluded.
4. Indication question: no discrete nodule can be identified and matched on both films, so change in the surveillance nodule cannot be judged from these images. The prior report's nodular opacity and small pleural effusion are not confirmed on the images.
5. Cardiac silhouette appears enlarged on the AP current film (F3). Indeterminate, not comparable with the PA prior.
6. Prominent aortic knuckle, with the upper mediastinum looking wider on the AP current film (F5). Indeterminate. The two blind reads disagreed (stable versus indeterminate). Widening is not called as a change.
7. Coarse linear and reticular markings in the left mid and lower zones, similar distribution on both films (F6). Stable by one of two reads.

RECOMMENDATIONS:
- CT chest, with contrast if appropriate, to address the right lower zone opacity, right hilum, nodule surveillance, small nodules and pleural questions. The findings do not specify an interval, so timing is for the attending to set.
- Repeat PA and lateral chest radiographs with adequate exposure and good inspiration when the patient is able. The findings do not specify an interval.
- Lateral or right lateral decubitus view, or ultrasound of the right base or right upper quadrant, for the possible subpulmonic effusion and diaphragm contour question.
- Echocardiography if heart size is clinically relevant.
- Review the source images in PACS with windowing, as the images were downsampled.

AI DRAFT: requires resident review and attending signature.
